name: Stochastic oversold cross-up in an uptrend (Pine import)
rationale: Faithful import of the Stochastic-crossover-in-trend strategy (Alorse 'Stoch RSI Crossover Strat + EMA' / Trade Pro: %K crosses up through %D inside the oversold zone while a stacked EMA ribbon confirms an uptrend; 3:1 ATR-based risk). Economic mechanism: the stochastic oscillator measures where price sits within its recent high-low range; a %K-over-%D cross UP from the oversold zone signals that a short-term pullback has stopped going down and momentum is turning back up — and gating that turn on an established uptrend (EMA ribbon stacked, price above a long MA) restricts it to BUYING THE DIP within a trend rather than catching a falling knife. The edge is the timing of re-entry on a trend pullback, captured precisely by the cross. The distinct structural piece vs our other reversion specs: the entry uses the cross_up OPERATOR on the range_position feature (a Donchian/stochastic channel-position read in [0,1]) through a low oversold floor — a TURN trigger, not a static level — combined with a MaTrendFilter uptrend gate (setup.ma_trend_filter). Our existing range-floor spec buys a STATIC low position in a COMPRESSED range (a grid/mean-reversion regime); this instead buys the MOMENT range_position turns up out of oversold while in a TREND — a different trigger (cross vs level) and a different regime (trend vs chop). Translation losses (noted, not fabricated): (1) the registry exposes a single channel-position series (range_position), not separate smoothed %K and %D lines — the %K-cross-%D event is approximated by range_position crossing UP through a fitted oversold floor (the position itself turning up out of oversold), with the Finder fitting the lookback and floor; (2) the multi-EMA ribbon alignment (8>14>50) collapses to the single fitted-MA uptrend gate; (3) the literal ATR x3 stop becomes a fitted stop fraction (sizing/units stay with the master). Honest prior: stochastic-cross-in-trend is a staple retail setup; net of ~20bps on crypto spot it is unproven and prone to repeated small whipsaws on shallow pullbacks — expected a powered fail that maps the dip-re-entry surface; the Gate disposes. Disconfirmer: an RSI-overbought signal exit takes profit once the bounce matures; the stop + time-stop close a 'dip' that keeps falling (the uptrend was actually breaking — thesis wrong).
catalyst: stochastic channel-position crosses up out of oversold while price is in a confirmed uptrend
